item.title: Bayern confirm major Díaz injury blow after Arsenal draw
item.description: Bayern confirm major Díaz injury blow after Arsenal draw After coming on as a second-half substitute in Bayern Munich’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League, Luis Díaz was forced off again towards the end of the match. FC Bayern have now confirmed that medical examinations revealed a muscle fibre tear in the Colombia international’s left hamstring. How long will Luis Diaz be out injured? As a result of the injury, Díaz will be “sidelined for the foreseeable future”, the German champions announced. According to Bild, the 29-year-old is expected to be out of action for between four and six weeks. Consequently, Díaz is set to miss Bayern’s upcoming fixtures against Freiburg, Magdeburg, Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid and Mainz, as well as Colombia’s international matches in November. Meanwhile, he's a major doubt for Bayern’s games against 1. FC Köln, Lille and Hamburger SV following the international break.

item.title: Penguins forward Ben Kindel collapsed during team flight, will undergo treatment and testing
item.description: FILE - Pittsburgh Penguins center Ben Kindel plays in the third period of an NHL hockey game against the Washington Capitals, Oct. 7, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Nick Wass, File) Nick Wass The Pittsburgh Penguins gave an update Thursday on the status of forward Ben Kindel, who experienced a medical episode on a plane. Previous coverage >>> Penguins forward Ben Kindel hospitalized after medical emergency on team flight Kyle Dubas, president of hockey operations and general manager for the Penguins, spoke during a press conference at the UPMC Lemieux Sports Complex. Kindel, 19, collapsed about 10 minutes into the Penguins’ return flight from Salt Lake City on Tuesday, Dubas said. The collapse has since been diagnosed as a vasovagal episode. The Mayo Clinic describes a vasovagal episode as when “your heart rate and blood pressure ... drop suddenly. That leads to reduced blood flow to your brain, causing you to briefly lose consciousness.” The Penguins medical director was on the flight and tended to Kindel along with other staff. Kindel was given oxygen and regained consciousness. Dubas said the flight performed an emergency medical landing back in Salt Lake City, where paramedics met the plane and took Kindel to the University of Utah Medical Center for further treatment. Kindel was cleared Wednesday to travel back to Pittsburgh and was at the Lemieux Sports Complex for treatment and testing Thursday, Dubas said. He will be placed on the injured reserve list. “We will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben. That’s our primary goal and paramount to his future and health,” Dubas said. This is a developing story. Check back for updates as more information becomes available. item.description: With the New England Patriots set to take on the Chicago Bears in Week 7 on Thursday night, it’s time to make start or sit decisions on running backs Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson in fantasy football . That said, it was more of the same for Henderson last week, as he had yet another disappointing showing with 40 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Stevenson also had a lackluster showing, as he didn’t record a single catch and finished with just 36 yards on 14 carries. item.title: Angel Reese's 4-word message makes Valkyries' WNBA Finals reality clear
item.description: Angel Reese's 4-word message makes Valkyries' WNBA Finals reality clear originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It started early for Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream . To begin Game 3 at a raucous State Farm Arena in Atlanta, the Dream held the Golden State Valkyries without a point for more than half of the opening quarter. Though the Valkyries would keep it close and rally to tie the game with a strong start to the third quarter, the Dream would pull away again, as an inspired Reese led Atlanta to a 97-71 victory on Wednesday night. After a tight Game 1 loss in San Francisco, Reese pledged to be more aggressive and get downhill against the Valkyries' lauded defense. She has done just that, building a Finals MVP-worthy resume with three successive double-doubles. MORE : Angel Reese sends Valkyries message after WNBA Finals Game 3 blowout win But even Reese has accrued 51 points and 28 rebounds in Games 2 and 3, it is her attitude as well as her counting stats that is putting Golden State at a disadvantage. Midway through the second quarter of Game 3, Reese took a pass at the top of the key from Jordin Canada and found herself isolated against Golden State big Aminata Gueye. It seems Reese has made it her personal mission to disrupt Gueye; the two have jawed back and forth throughout the series so far. After Reese attacked the paint and bullied Gueye out of the way for a layup, she backpedaled to her spot on defense while yelling "you can't guard me" at the rookie center with all of seven games' experience in the WNBA. Angel Reese: "You can't guard me! You can't guard me!" Kate Scott has the WNBA Finals Game 3 play-by-play call for NBC Sports. 🏀🎙️ https://t.co/mj63IgWXzy — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 22, 2026 It speaks to how Reese is taking it upon herself to set the tone and bully the Valkyries at every opportunity -- even from the bench in a 25-point game. The intensity is defining this series but tilting it in Atlanta's favor after three games. Golden State has to find a way to slow down Reese and the Dream's runaway train in Game 4 to even the series. Otherwise, Atlanta will head out west with a chance to close out the Finals -- and its first-ever WNBA title -- next week. item.title: Gattuso Has Only One Request to Lazio Management Ahead of January Window
item.description: Gattuso Has Only One Request to Lazio Management Ahead of January Window Lazio might be set for a quiet January transfer session, but this wouldn’t be an issue for their head coach Gennaro Gattuso. Lazio Risk Another Transfer Ban The Biancocelesti had an eventful summer transfer campaign, signing seven new players. Angelo Fabiani’s savvy business didn’t cost the club’s coffers a large amount, as the deals were conducted on free transfers (Pedraza, Doekhi, and Sutalo), loans with obligation to buy (Frattesi, Sutalo, and Gudmundsson), or permanent transfers with innovative formulas (Pinamonti). Rating Lazio 2026 Summer Transfer Campaign: The Zero-Cost Masterclass And yet, Lazio are still struggling to balance their accounts and reach the required 0.7 cost-to-revenue ratio. Observers believe the club’s current figures are at circa 0.82, placing them well over the threshold. Therefore, the Aquile are bracing themselves for another transfer ban, similar to the summer of 2025, or at least a restricted (net-zero) transfer campaign, like the summer of 2026. Gennaro Gattuso Wants His Lazio Squad Intact According to Il Messaggero (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), market restrictions wouldn’t pose an issue for Gattuso, who is happy to march on with the current squad until the end of the season. The Calabrian coach has already built a solid group in his first few months at the club, with everyone steering in the same direction, as illustrated by their extraordinary start to the campaign. Can Lazio Avoid January Sales? As the Roman newspaper explains, Gattuso’s only request to the Lazio hierarchy is to avoid selling any important players like they did last January, when they cashed in on Matteo Guendouzi and Taty Castellanos, much to Maurizio Sarri’s dismay. Therefore, it remains to be seen whether the management will be willing to grant the 48-year-old his simple wish. The source points out that a few January exits might be deemed necessary to register capital gains and avoid a transfer ban in the summer of 2027.

item.title: CME bubble players making moves early at LPGA's BMW Championship
item.description: Karis Davidson came into the BMW Championship clinging to one of the last spots in the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship. With an $11 million purse and a $4 million first-place prize, gaining entry into the 60-player field is a high priority for LPGA players. Australia's Davidson, who currently ranks 59th on the Race to CME Globe, opened with a 6-under 66 at Pine Beach Golf Links, known as the Pebble Beach of South Korea, on a cold, windy day. "It was just kind of one of those perfect days with my irons and hybrids, that I nearly had a hole-in-one on the first birdie on the front nine," said Davidson, who holds a share of the lead with Japan's Yuri Yoshida. Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, one of the longest players in the game, shot 67 to hold a share of third with world No. 3 Haeran Ryu, Lauren Coughlin and Lucy Li. Lopez Ramirez entered the week 71st in the rankings and said she killed time during a slow day on the course playing Sudoku in between shots. She also soaked in the scenery. "Especially when it's blue skies out here, the views are insane," said Lopez Ramirez. "It's so pretty and so many trees and the greens and little islands. You lose your mind going in there." It's quite pretty." Li entered the week 69th on the CME rankings. She birdied all the par 5s in her opening 67. Carlota Ciganda, Lopez Ramirez's partner at the Solheim Cup , came into the week No. 60 on the CME points list after a fifth-place finish last week in China, where she incurred a two-stroke penalty for slow play . Ciganda shot 69 on Thursday in South Korea and holds a share of eighth. Coughlin double-bogeyed the fifth hole to get to 2 over early and then made seven birdies coming in to finish 5 under. She had 28 putts on the day. View this post on Instagram Ryu, a two-time major winner this year who recently won on the KLPGA, recorded one of four bogey-free rounds. She hit 17 greens in regulation, leading the field in that category with Angel Yin. Ryu made birdie on her only missed green of the day, the par-4 fifth. The BMW is the second of four no-cut events in the LPGA's fall Asia swing. The cutoff for the CME falls at the conclusion of next month's Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican in Belleair, Florida, giving players four more opportunities to make their moves. Beth Ann Nichols is a Golfweek senior writer covering the LPGA and women's golf. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: CME bubble players making moves early at LPGA's BMW Championship

item.title: Diogo Dalot: Italian paper sends Man United summer 2027 warning
item.description: Diogo Dalot: Italian paper sends Man United summer 2027 warning Diogo Dalot may be playing his final season at Manchester United, according to the latest reports from Italy. The Portuguese full-back, who joined United in 2018, is under contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2028. There have been whispers of an extension, yet talks remain at an early stage and no concrete progress has been made. Dalot unsure about future at Manchester United However, news emerging from Italy suggests that securing a new deal will prove difficult. Gazzetta dello Sport reports: “Dalot is 27 years old, in the prime of his career, and not playing in the Champions League could push him to leave the Premier League and return to Italy.” The paper goes on to explain that three Italian heavyweights have already enquired about him, while noting the impression he left during his loan spell at San Siro: “Serie A has never forgotten him, and he has already been discussed on several occasions: Roma attempted to sign him in the past, offering United a loan with a mandatory option to buy, but ultimately failed to find the right formula to convince the English club. “AC Milan, Inter and Juventus have already enquired about him: nothing concrete has been reached yet, but the player is popular, and discussions could be explored further down the line, especially if Manchester United can’t find the key to escape their current crisis.” If nothing changes quickly at United, they are unlikely to finish in the Champions League places. If Dalot wants to keep playing in the competition, he will almost certainly leave. His departure would leave United in a tricky position given his versatility. At the same time, it would give them the chance to refresh their full-back options. Alongside the left-back they are expected to sign, they could also target a right-back who better suits their style of play. Obvious replacement AS Roma’s Brazilian full-back Wesley, who is already on the Red Devils’ radar , would appear to be the ideal replacement. He is a technically gifted full-back, comfortable on either flank, which should make him every bit as valuable an asset as Dalot is to this side. The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 7/10 Why? ✅ With United’s planned 2027 defensive overhaul, a Dalot exit would hardly surprise ✅ His contract situation means the club must decide his future soon TPP View We believe that with the planned defensive overhaul, no one is safe, including Diogo Dalot . He may well be allowed to leave.

item.title: Philadelphia Union sign Neil Pierre to contract extension
item.description: Philadelphia Union sign Neil Pierre to contract extension By Jonathan Sigal TRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: Extension The Philadelphia Union have signed defender Neil Pierre to a new contract through the 2030-31 season with an option for 2031-32, the club announced Thursday. The 19-year-old center back initially signed with Philadelphia as a homegrown player ahead of the 2025 season, before joining Danish side Lyngby Boldklub on loan for the first half of the 2026 campaign. Since returning from loan, Pierre has become a locked-in starter with Philly. He has 4g/1a in 14 games, helping propel the Union up the Eastern Conference table during a historic unbeaten streak (12W-0L-3D) since the 2026 FIFA World Cup . Pierre recently earned his first three US men's national team caps, appearing alongside teammates Cavan Sullivan and Frankie Westfield to begin the 2030 World Cup cycle. He also placed No. 7 on MLS's annual 22 Under 22 Rankings , which recognize the league's top young players. "Neil is one of the brightest young center backs in our league, and he has consistently made the most of the opportunities he’s earned throughout his development within our club," said Philadelphia sporting director Jon Scheer. "His physical profile, ability to defend aggressively in 1v1 situations, and composure and confidence on the ball make him a model fit for both our game model and the demands of the modern game. He has taken significant steps forward this season, and his progression is another example of the pathway we’ve established from our academy through Union II to the first team. "We’re excited to extend his future with the club and look forward to supporting his continued development and growth." READ MORE: MLS Transfer Tracker

item.title: Emery not sure if Manzambi will win fitness battle to face Man City
item.description: Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Aston Villa and Fenerbahce at Villa Park. (is associated with: «Emery not sure if Manzambi will win fitness battle to face Man City») David Davies/PA Wire/dpa Unai Emery has warned his Aston Villa side they "must be ready" for the challenge against unbeaten leaders Manchester City on Saturday with or without Johan Manzambi. The 21-year-old has made a lightning start to life in England and has registered three goals and three assists in his first six appearances in a Villa shirt. Manzambi missed Villa’s 3-1 Champions League victory over Viking on Wednesday and Emery, who initially described Manzambi’s injury as “small”, now says he does not know whether the Switzerland international will be ready to face City. After the game, the Villa boss was asked what the situation is with Manzambi, and he replied: “I don’t know now. “Tomorrow we will see how are the players and Saturday is in a few days but we must be ready, in case he is not, to keep being consistent as a team collectively. “Individually today I think some players did a clear step forward. So, in case Manzambi is there on Saturday, fantastic. If he is not, wait for the next match. Now, I don’t know if he’s going to be available for Saturday.” Alejandro Garnacho’s lack of playing time has also been a talking point this season but Wednesday also saw more minutes for the ex-Chelsea and Manchester United winger. The 22-year-old stepped off the bench in the 72nd minute for his second appearance in a week and he could have got his first goal but was denied by Arild Ostbo. Emery says Garnacho had his best game for the club. He added: “Garnacho as well, playing 20 minutes. He played his best minutes with us as well, so it is positive. Let’s go.” Brazilian winger Alysson put in an impressive performance on his first Champions League start and caused problems for the Viking defence all night. He contributed to Villa’s third goal when his cross bounced off Heggheim and into the back of the net and he took the congratulations off his team-mates. Giving his first interview in English to VillaTV, he said: “It was a dream night for me, for my family. I’m very proud, me and my team, my team-mates. The phrase is ‘dream night’. For me, it’s perfect. I’m very happy.”

item.title: Eustace reveals latest Derby County injury blow
item.description: Eustace reveals latest Derby County injury blow John Eustace has confirmed Derby County will be without captain Lewis Travis until next month, while Alex Mowatt remains a doubt for Saturday’s trip to Sheffield United. Travis suffered an ankle injury in last weekend’s defeat to Stoke City and has since undergone a scan. “Trav’s going to be out until after the next international break,” Eustace said. “That’s obviously a big blow to us over the next four games. “It’s a different injury from the one that kept him out before. He went in for a tackle, and he’s just gone over on his ankle, unfortunately.” Mowatt is also struggling ahead of the trip to Bramall Lane after cutting his foot in the defeat to QPR. “Alex will be touch-and-go for the weekend,” Eustace added. “He hasn’t really trained yet, so we’ll have to wait and see with him. He had a bad cut to the foot, and he’s had stitches in that, so we’ll see on that.” Free agent signing Jack Robinson is pushing to be involved soon, meanwhile. “It won’t take him too long to get up to speed,” Eustace said. “He’s a very experienced pro. He’s still kept himself in good shape, so let’s wait and see.”

item.title: Tokyo Marathon winner handed six-year doping ban for submitting fake prescription
item.description: One of the world’s top marathon runners has been given a six-year ban from the sport after submitting a fake prescription to attempt to explain a positive drug test. Ruti Aga, who won the Tokyo Marathon in 2019, returned a positive test for the banned substance methylprednisolone, a steroid which is used to reduce pain, after winning a half-marathon in China in March. The Ethiopian claimed she had been prescribed the drug to treat a knee injury which she had been suffering from since April 2015. But an investigation into her test by the Ethiopian Anti-Doping Authority revealed that the prescription she submitted came from a medical clinic which did not actually exist, and was issued to her by a family member who had “no medical registration with the relevant authority”. Aga was charged with violating three anti-doping regulations but did not respond to the charges before the deadline, which could potentially have taken a year off her suspension if she admitted the breaches. The ban was therefore issued without a hearing. The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday that it had banned Aga for two years for the positive test and a further four years, to be served consecutively, for “tampering” with the investigation. Aga attempted “to mislead the investigation by providing false information in an interview” in April and produced a “forged/manipulated document” in May, according to the AIU’s press release on the case. The 32-year-old was ranked 11th in the world at the time of testing positive and as well as claiming the Tokyo title in 2019 had four top-three finishes at World Marathon Majors. The AIU’s chief executive, Brett Clothier, said: “Protecting clean competition takes resources, but this case sends a clear message: attempts to cheat will be exposed”.

item.title: Section 2 soccer playoffs: What to watch in today's postseason action
item.description: The image depicts a soccer player controlling the ball with their feet. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The opening week of the 2026 sectional soccer tournaments continues today with first-round and quarterfinal action throughout Section 2. Fifteen girls' soccer first-round contests will be held, while ten first-round and quarterfinal games will take place in the boys' soccer tournament. Top games Class AAA boys - No. 5 Albany at No. 4 Saratoga Springs, 7 p.m.: These Suburban Council foes tied 2-2 in late September and finished the regular season with identical plus-13 goal differentials. They now meet for a Class AAA semifinal berth. Saratoga (7-6-1) lost five of its final six games, with the lone win coming against top-seeded Shaker. Albany (7-5-4) won once in its last five, beating No. 6 Colonie. The winner will face Shaker on Monday. Class AA boys - No. 5 Queensbury at No. 4 Niskayuna, 5 p.m.: Niskayuna (6-6-2) beat Foothills Council champion Queensbury (8-3-5) in their only regular-season meeting. Queensbury finished with a plus-18 goal differential but went 0-2-1 against Suburban Council opponents. Nisky lost four of its final five games, finishing with a plus-2 differential. The winner is likely to face top-seeded Bethlehem, the state's No. 2-ranked team, in Monday's semifinals. Class C girls - No. 14 Bolton/Warrensburg at No. 3 Schoharie, 6 p.m.: Schoharie (15-1) has won seven straight since its only loss of the season to Mayfield. Led by sisters Evelyn and Alayna Messner, who have combined for 78 of Schoharie's Section 2-leading 102 goals, the Storm seeks a better opening-round performance after an 8-1 loss to Waterford last year. Bolton/Warrensburg (4-10-2), winless since beating Class D Hadley-Luzerne in late September, faces a challenge just to advance past the first round. Player to watch Cooper Bibighaus, Loudonville Christian boys: The Eagles' offensive catalyst, Bibighaus, can both finish chances and create them, likely making him the focal point of No. 14 Galway's defense when it meets No. 3 Loudonville Christian today. In one week this October, Bibighaus scored a hat trick against Mekeel Christian Academy, recorded six assists against Johnstown, and added two goals and two assists against Fonda-Fultonville. His vision, movement and precise delivery on passes, corner kicks and crosses make him difficult to contain, even when opponents build their defensive plans around him. item.title: 76ers predicted to sign ex-Lakers disappointing first-round pick, former LeBron James teammate
item.description: 76ers predicted to sign ex-Lakers disappointing first-round pick, former LeBron James teammate originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers put themselves in a difficult spot after making so many moves during the summer that they ended up with one player over the roster limit. For some time, it seemed clear that Dalton Knecht was going to be the odd man out. LA was pretty much set with its roster heading into the preseason, and Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed what changed for Knecht. “I think the biggest thing is the team changed. The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he's gotten better as a player the last two years. I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he's in a tough spot right now," Redick said. Earlier in the week, every team around the league had to make cuts to get its roster down to the required limit. LA ultimately decided to officially waive Knecht. “The Los Angeles Lakers are waiving 2024 No. 17 pick Dalton Knecht, sources tell ESPN,” ESPN’s Shams Charania wrote. There is interest from multiple teams around the league in potentially signing Knecht to a two-way contract. Knox News’ Wynton Jackson believes Knecht will sign with the Philadelphia 76ers and reunite with LeBron James. “Early in Knecht's rookie year with the Lakers, he erupted for 37 points in a win over the Utah Jazz . His teammate, LeBron James, famously criticized opposing NBA teams for allowing the Lakers to draft Knecht at No. 17. James is now with the Philadelphia 76ers for one last title run before he retires. The Sixers have a deeper roster and championship aspirations. However, it's unlikely that James, 41, and the oft-injured 2023 MVP Joel Embiid will play the entire 82-game regular season schedule. Philadelphia could take a flier on Knecht to step in when its two superstars rest, and his shooting ability could swing a playoff game,” Jackson wrote. There is no doubt that Knecht was dealt a bad hand in LA, but he now has an opportunity to join a team that could give him a chance to prove himself. The 76ers' main rotation may be difficult to crack, but Knecht could have opportunities to show what he can do when the roster is shorthanded. All he needs is a chance to prove he belongs in the NBA. item.title: Houston Texans icon J.J. Watt agrees to multi-year deal as CBS' lead analyst for NFL broadcasts
item.description: J.J. Watt's move to lead analyst for CBS is for the long term after he agreed to a multi-year deal to team with Jim Nantz. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) Former Houston Texans star J.J. Watt has a new multi-year deal to serve as the lead analyst for the NFL on CBS, the network announced Thursday. Watt will remain paired with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson as CBS' lead announcing team, which will call Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta after the 2027 season. "I've had a front-row seat to J.J.'s growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his hall-of-fame playing career," said David Berson, the global sports chairman of Skydance, CBS' parent company. "He's insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels. We are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage." After his 12 years in the NFL, including 10 with the Texans, Watt joined CBS in 2023 as a studio analyst. He made the leap to the booth last season and drew rave reviews partnering with Ian Eagle on CBS's No. 2 crew. When Tony Romo was placed on leave and later parted ways with CBS after a driving under the influence arrest, Watt moved up to lead analyst in late July. "I am incredibly honored and grateful to have the opportunity to represent CBS Sports and all of the fantastic people who make this place so special," Watt said. "From the brotherhood of The NFL Today to my crews calling games, I couldn't ask for better teammates alongside me on this television journey. I am thankful to David Berson for his leadership, vision and trust. I love this job and can't wait to see ya Sunday with Jim and Tracy and many more Sundays to come!" Watt was a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and was honored as the 2017 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year with the Texans. He was inducted into the franchise's Ring of Honor in 2023 and is expected to be a first-ballot electee to the Pro Football Hall of Fame when he becomes eligible in January 2028. Selected 11th overall by Houston in the first round of the 2011 NFL draft out of Wisconsin, Watt played 12 seasons with the Texans (2011-20) and Arizona Cardinals (2021-22). A five-time first team All-Pro and five-time Pro Bowl selection, he is the only player in NFL history to record multiple seasons with at least 20 sacks and finished his career with 114 ½ sacks. item.title: James Cook has improved efficiency from 2025, even against heavier boxes
item.description: Believe it or not, James Cook has had a better start to 2026 than a season ago when he led the NFL in rushing yards. And he’s done it despite defenses placing a relatively high priority on stopping him. Through six games in 2025, the Buffalo Bills feature back had rushed for 537 yards at a 5.0 yards-per-carry clip. Through six games this season, Cook has 627 yards on the ground at a 5.4 yards-per-carry clip. At this point of the season last year, Cook had seen 89.7% of his runs against seven or more defenders in the box. On those runs, he averaged 5.08 yards per tote and had a 10-plus yard run rate of 12.4%. This season, the percentage of Cook runs with seven-plus box defenders is up to 92.3%. He’s averaged 5.34 yards per carry on those runs with a 10-plus yard run rate of 21.9%. My word. Beyond his incredible efficiency improvement from the high bar set in 2025, Cook has also been excellent this season against seven or more defenders in the box relative to his running back contemporaries. Through Week 6, there’ve been 38 running backs who’ve carried the football 40 or more times against seven or more defenders in the box. Here’s where Cook ranks in many rushing categories in those scenarios: 108 carries (2nd) 577 rushing yards (2nd) 5.34 yards per carry (3rd) 21.9% explosive run rate (1st) 55.6% success rate – 6th He is 30th in yards after contact per rush in those scenarios at 1.82 yards. But that’s never been Cook’s speciality. His subtle cutting skills, flexibility, and breakaway speed are how he wins, although he has added more power and wherewithal through contact as he’s developed in Buffalo. And I cannot finish this article before a noticeable hat tip to the Bills offensive line. Against seven or more box defenders, Cook’s 3.52 yards before contact is far and away the highest average in the league. The running back’s own elusiveness is a factor there too. There’s plenty of football left this season. But right now, after winning the rushing title a year ago, Cook has actually gotten more efficient toting the rock. And he’s been among the league’s best even when the opposing defense is making a concerted effort to stop him by not providing him light boxes. Stats courtesy of Fantasy Points Data*

item.title: ‘Very easy explanation’ – Tom Brady speaks on the Patriots overtaking the Bills in his power rankings
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Tom Brady has placed the New England Patriots fourth in his latest NFL power rankings after Week 6. The Patriots were last in action on Sunday, securing a 26-19 win over the New York Jets. That victory means they are second in the AFC East (4-2) behind the Buffalo Bills, who have a 5-1 record after beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. But despite the Bills having the better record right now, Tom Brady has still placed New England above them in his latest NFL power rankings. He put the Bills in fifth and the Patriots in fourth and said there’s an easy explanation why. Speaking to Fox, he said: “That’s right, New England jumps Buffalo this week. Listen, there’s a very easy explanation for this. In the Tom Brady power rankings, there’s a clear scenario for when the head-to-head tie-breaker applies. It’s situations where I, Tom Brady, feel like applying it.” He added: “Drake [Maye], he’s been on fire the last three games. He’s calm in the pocket, making throws in big moments and taking care of the ball. “Does this team remind you of last year’s Pats all of a sudden? I think so.” The rest of Brady’s top five is made up by the Minnesota Vikings (third), the Kansas City Chiefs (second) and the San Francisco 49ers (first). He’s stuck in a mundane feud with Randy Orton that feels like a retread of their failed WrestleMania feud from earlier this year that was ruined by Pat McAfee. The main crux of Orton vs. Rhodes has been whether or not Rhodes is willing to embrace his darker side. On last week’s SmackDown, Rhodes did just that (kind of, sort of) when he punt kicked Baron Corbin. Still, Rhodes remains a babyface on TV, though he has expressed his willingness to turn heel if the story dictates . Soon, perhaps it will. According to WrestleVotes on Fightful , “The early WrestleMania 43 creative discussions are underway and include Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns and CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes.” WWE fans just saw Punk vs. Rhodes back in August in a battle between two of WWE’s top three babyfaces, but those dynamics could soon change. With WWE looking to run back Punk vs. Rhodes again, perhaps at WrestleMania 43, the company absolutely must turn one of those stars heel if that’s the case. Punk is the obvious option because he’s been so successful as a villain in the past. Rhodes, though, is the better option. It was clear, after all, that Punk was the more liked of the two stars in their SummerSlam match, and turning Rhodes heel in the near future would be perfect timing. Rhodes is stale, the WWE product needs a jolt of excitement, and the company has a ton of top babyfaces, ranging from Oba Femi to Penta to Kevin Owens to Roman Reigns, who can carry the fan favorite flag if Rhodes turns. As WWE fans continue to feel that Rhodes fatigue, the creative team may be forced to do something drastic to get him back on track. The most drastic change for Rhodes wouldn’t be simply embracing his dark side. It would be actually moving to the dark side once and for all. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
